title: GeoJSON Minified Size Calculator: Byte Truth
description: Estimate a GeoJSON file's byte size after compact serialization with the GeoJSON Minified Size Calculator — before you minify. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a sample collection that occupies 1,521 bytes pretty-printed estimates at 669 bytes minified — a 56.0% saving you can quote before touching the file.
quick_answer: The GeoJSON Minified Size Calculator estimates the byte size of a GeoJSON document after compact serialization — whitespace stripped, structure untouched. Paste the GeoJSON and read the projected size and the saving: the number that decides whether minifying is worth it, computed before you commit to the compact file.

Two exports of the same data differ mysteriously in size. Minified estimates normalise the comparison: same air removed, real difference exposed.
Minified size is the input to the gzip question — if the compact file is already small, compression infrastructure may be ceremony.
Students meet the idea that formatting is bytes: a 56% whitespace share in a real file teaches it permanently.
Every space, tab and newline outside strings is air; everything inside quotes is data and untouchable. The estimate is a re-serialization, not a guess: parse, print compactly, count bytes.
